name: Lieutenant Hanna
role: Pilot in Larry's unit; Larry says killed in 1968
summary: A young pilot Larry flew with, named while he was looking at VN-0046, rice paddies he thinks he photographed "taking off from Ton Son Nhut": "Lieutenant Hanna, he was 19 or 20. He was kind of cross eyed… he was a real good pilot. I flew with him a couple times." "Hanna was part of my Unit." After Larry left, he says, Hanna went on to another unit and was "killed in 1968 Kontom which is a bout 50 miles south of Pleikeu."
researchNotes: New on 2026-09-05 (data/recollections/giscus-vn-0046-c18308860.json). Two checks run, both negative, recorded so they are not repeated. (1) 2026-09-05, the helicopter pilots' memorial roll (sources/vhpa-kia-index): two men of this surname, neither fits: one was killed in 1968 with the division Larry names, but was born in 1948 and reached Vietnam in November 1967, so he was sixteen in 1965 and cannot have flown with Larry; the other died in 1969 on a first tour that began that year. Neither died near Kontum. (2) 2026-09-12, the full U.S. casualty file (DCAS, all ~58,000 records): all 13 Hanna and Hannah entries read; apart from the warrant-officer pilot already ruled out on age, the only 1968 officer among them was a Marine Corps infantry second lieutenant. No entry of either spelling was found to fit a pilot of Larry's unit (the pass did not record places of death for each entry). That leaves: the death belongs to another man, or the memory of his death is wrong, or a detail (rank, year, place, spelling) is off. The spelling Hana was not in that pass. Details, and why no candidate first name is written in any record: research/people/lt-hanna.md. In the same comment Larry said he put the first radio beacon in at Pleiku, and that the base there was called the golf course; the base known by that name was at An Khê from September 1965, after he left. Held against the unit question, not pursued here. Ledger #31, issue #126.
